subject: Post-call: data sovereignty & region-pinning Q&A (next steps)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Wright <sophia.wright@novahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: data sovereignty & region-pinning Q&A (next steps)

Hi Sophia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the open items we agreed to follow up on regarding data handling, residency, and failover behavior. I’ve attached a short summary and a residency matrix for reference.

Summary of what we covered:
- Primary ask: NovaHealth wants all production inference workloads and logs to remain in the EU for EU patients; US workloads for US patients.
- Concern: cross-region failover and backups — what happens to backups and logs if the primary region becomes unavailable?
- Compliance: whether PII ever leaves the pinned region for processing, logs, or snapshots.
- Ops: retention controls (snapshots, audit logs), and whether we can provide proof points (SOC 2 artifacts, architecture diagrams).

Open items / next steps I’ll own:
1) Confirm default and configurable behaviour for region pinning + failover (answer below).
2) Provide written guidance on backups and snapshot replication options (attached).
3) Share a short checklist of controls around logging (what we log, masking options, in-region retention).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Monica (solutions eng) to go over your network & KMS requirements.

Quick answers (high level):
- Region pinning: you can pin a workspace/model to a single region (EU or US). When pinned, inference compute and persistent storage are kept in-region.
- Failover: we support configurable failover policies. By default, failover to a secondary region is opt-in; if enabled, all failover traffic goes to a pre-authorized region variant (e.g., EU -> US). We can also keep failover disabled so that requests fail with a clear error rather than moving data across borders.
- Backups/snapshots: snapshots are encrypted at rest and can be configured to remain in-region. Cross-region replication is optional and requires an explicit configuration and contract clause.
- Logs & analytics: audit logs can be kept in-region; application telemetry that contains PII can be redacted before export. We have log-forwarding integrations if you want to send logs to your SIEM in the same region.

Attachments: redwood_region_pinning_summary.pdf (short explainer), residency_matrix.csv (per-resource defaults), SOC2-evidence-stub.txt (summary of artifacts we can share).

Proposed immediate actions:
- Confirm whether NovaHealth requires failover to be disabled by default (so we can prepare a mutual action plan).
- Are there any particular data classes or datasets (by product or endpoint) you want pinned differently?
- Would you like a 60-minute deep-dive with Monica next week? I proposed Wed/Thu afternoons below.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your priorities and will loop in Stephanie (contracts) if you want residency language added to the MSA up front.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks, Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions before we lock in the deep-dive: 

1) Encryption: is the customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) option supported in EU regions? If so, are key operations (wrap/unwrap) performed in-region or do they go to a global KMS endpoint?
2) Backups: if we enable backups but keep "in-region" flagged, are backups ever staged temporarily in another region during maintenance or restore? We must avoid any temporary copy outside EU for EU-pinned data.
3) Logs: you mentioned telemetry redaction. Can you confirm the default retention for audit logs and whether we can request a hardened retention policy (e.g., 90 days with immediate purge option)?
4) Failover behavior: if we opt-in to failover to the US, will logs and snapshots created during failover be written back to the EU once the EU region is back online, or will they persist in the US?

Also, can you put an initial residency clause suggestion in writing that Stephanie/your legal team can review? We want something short in the SOW/MSA that covers: data location guarantees, backups, and cross-region failover opt-in.

Amit and I are available for Wed 2026-05-06 14:00-15:00 UTC or Thu 2026-05-07 09:00-10:00 UTC for the technical call.

Best,
Sophia Wright

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Amit Rao <amit.rao@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: data sovereignty & region-pinning Q&A (next steps)

Sophia — great questions. Answers below (keeping it operational and actionable). Monica included for the deep-dive scheduling and KMS specifics; Stephanie included to start a draft residency clause.

1) KMS: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in EU regions. Key operations are performed against the region's KMS endpoint when you use a regional KMS (e.g., your cloud provider KMS in eu-west-1). If you elect Redwood-managed multi-region KMS, key metadata may be visible in our control plane, but cryptographic operations remain in-region when resources are pinned. Monica will share the exact flow and the minimal set of KMS permissions we require.

2) Backups/snapshots: snapshots are by default created in-region and retained there. During planned platform maintenance we do not stage EU-pinned snapshots outside the pinned region. For disaster recovery, cross-region replication is an explicit option that requires both parties' sign-off and an accompanying config flag — we will not replicate EU-pinned snapshots to US unless you enable that.

3) Logs & retention: default audit-log retention is 180 days. We can support a hardened retention (90 days) and an immediate purge workflow for on-demand data deletion requests; both can be added to the SOW. Sensitive fields are redacted by default in telemetry exports; if you need PII removed at the source we can enable pre-export masking.

4) Failover behavior: if you opt into automatic failover to a secondary region, inference requests will be served from the secondary region during the outage and any artifacts (temporary caches, logs generated during failover) will be stored in the active region. On recovery we offer two modes: (a) "replicate-back" where we copy artifacts back to the primary region and reconcile state, or (b) "leave-in-secondary" where artifacts remain in the secondary. Replicate-back is available but must be enabled and time-bounded in the runbook to avoid unexpected cross-border transfers.

Action items / proposals:
- Monica will run a 60-minute technical deep-dive to validate KMS flows and network requirements. Proposed slots: Wed 2026-05-06 14:00-15:00 UTC or Thu 2026-05-07 09:00-10:00 UTC (choose one).
- Stephanie will draft a short residency clause and circulate a redline by EOD Tue 2026-05-05.
- I’ll prepare a short MOP (maintenance & failover playbook) that documents the replicate-back option and the conditions that trigger it.

If these answers look good I’ll proceed and attach the MOP draft and residency clause for review before the technical call.

Cheers,
Ben
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
